candidates.title: Scheduled pages are promoted on a request after their due time
candidates.preconditions: A page created with a future publication timestamp; controlled application clock fixture.
candidates.gherkinScenario:
Feature: Content Scheduling
  Scenario: Scheduled pages are promoted on a request after their due time
    Given the administrator is logged into Bludit admin dashboard
    When the administrator creates a page with title "Scheduled Announcement" and future date
    Then the page is saved with status "scheduled" and is hidden from public blog
    When the application clock advances past the scheduled publication time
    And a visitor requests the public site home page
    Then the page "Scheduled Announcement" status changes to "published"
    And the page title "Scheduled Announcement" is visible on the public blog listing
candidates.fixture: Setup: Clean clock/dbPages fixture. Teardown: Remove scheduled page.

oracle.observable: Database page entry status transitions from scheduled to published; page renders in published public collection.

sourceRefs.note: scheduler promotes due entries to published
invokes page scheduler on request boot

novelty.rationale: Proposal targeting unexercised behavior beyond baseline. Baseline overlap analysis: BL-017 changes post date but never tests request-time scheduler promotion to published status.

baselineOverlap.rationale: BL-017 changes post date but never tests request-time scheduler promotion to published status.
baselineOverlap.comparisonBasis: Reconciled with 257 features, 258 test suites, 359 assertions in bewt-original/

candidates.negativeControl: A draft page with future date remains draft and is not published by scheduler.

humanDecision.rationale: Human-in-the-loop batch approval by Team Lead for implementation in BEWT-CovExt v2.0 Final Completion Sprint.

candidates.title: Static status maps to page type and the static-page collection
candidates.preconditions: Admin authenticated; no existing static page with slug 'about-our-team'.
candidates.gherkinScenario:
Feature: Page Type Classification
  Scenario: Static status maps to page type and the static-page collection
    Given the administrator is logged into Bludit admin
    When the administrator creates content titled "About Our Team"
    And changes the status to "Static" in the advanced options
    And clicks "Save"
    Then the content is stored in the static pages collection
    And "About Our Team" appears in the static navigation menu
    And "About Our Team" does NOT appear in the chronological blog post stream
